props.title: Foam: noise in Godot 4.7.2
props.note: ClassDB on Godot 4.7.2 · docs function list · 2026-10-16

B13.visual_intent: Act title 'Foam' in the table heading; three rows: the shading language's function list (no noise function), the visual shader's 110 nodes (no Voronoi or noise node, only random range), and the FastNoiseLite resource (yes, a Cellular type).
B13.motion_claim: Rows light one at a time; the first two answer 'none', the third 'yes'.
B13.why: The claim is a count and a lookup in the engine itself; a table with the counted number is the evidence.

B14.visual_intent: A grid of six by four outline squares (the series pixel-grid cast) on the cream stage; one terracotta dot (grey-ringed) drops into each of the 24 squares at a different spot; then two neighbouring dots are joined by a thin line and a dashed grey line (the perpendicular bisector between them) is drawn with the label 'equally close'. Labels: 'one point each'. Drawn, not rendered: labelled 'drawing'.
B14.motion_claim: Dots land one per square; then the line of equal distance grows between two neighbours.
B14.runner_up: ShaderLab: the real points render first
B14.why: The plan is a picture of squares and points; the real render of the same idea follows in the next beat.

cues.label: dot: multiply matching parts, add them up
sine: a smooth wave between -1 and 1
fract: the part after the point: x minus floor(x)

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · top view · points circle
props.caption: hash: an address in, random-looking numbers out; same address, same numbers

B15.capture_spec: C08: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view of the plane, shader 03a-cells-debug show=0 (points and grid), cell_density 8, 1080 x 1080.
B15.visual_intent: Code card with the four hash lines (cues on dot, sine, fract); at right a real top view: pale squares with a grey grid and a small deep-blue dot in every square, the dots slowly circling.
B15.motion_claim: A dot sits in every square and slowly circles; the same square always has its dot in the same place.
B15.runner_up: manim: a hash drawn as a function box
B15.why: The real points are the hash's output; the code beside them shows what made them.

B16.visual_intent: The grid from the last act's cast. One pixel (a small cream dot with a dark ring) sits near the border of a square. The 3 by 3 block of squares around it is outlined; the nine points inside are marked and nine thin lines run from the pixel to them; the nearest line is drawn thick, the second nearest medium; labels 'nearest' and 'second'.
B16.motion_claim: The nine lines draw in, then all but two fade, leaving the nearest thick and the second nearest medium.
B16.why: Choosing a minimum among nine candidates is a picture of lines of different lengths; a drawing shows the competition.

cues.label: length: of an offset, the distance

B17.capture_spec: C09: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, shader 03a-cells-debug show=1 (the nearest distance as a grey ramp), 1080 x 1080. mean 0.43 is E7 (evidence/planning-checks).
B17.visual_intent: Code card with the eight loop lines (length line then the keep-two line lit); at right a real top view: a field of soft cones, pale at every point and deepening away from it, slowly moving; the pill 'mean 0.43' lands near the end.
B17.motion_claim: A field of cones: pale at each point, deepening away from it, while the points circle.
B17.why: The real nearest-distance field is the picture itself; a plot would describe one slice of it.

cues.label: c.y - c.x: second nearest minus nearest

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · top view · edge distance
props.caption: second nearest minus nearest: zero on the border between two points

B18.capture_spec: C10: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, shader 03a-cells-debug show=2 (second minus nearest as a ramp), 1080 x 1080.
B18.visual_intent: Code card (the cells return and the fragment's first lines, the foam line lit); at right a real top view: deep-blue cells whose borders are a thin pale net, moving as the points circle.
B18.motion_claim: Thin pale lines trace the borders between the cells and wobble as the points move.
B18.runner_up: manim: two circles and their equal-distance line
B18.why: The real edge map is the shape foam will take; a drawing of two circles would show the idea but not the net.

cues.label: smoothstep: eases from 0 to 1 between two edges
mix: blends from a to b; t of 0 gives a, 1 gives b

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · top view · width widens
props.caption: edge_width 0.02 widening to 0.1: foam covers about 13 % of the water

B19.capture_spec: C11: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, shader 03-noise-foam, edge_width 0.02 widening to 0.1 by 75 % of the beat; the 13 % figure is E7.
B19.visual_intent: Code card (the fragment: foam line then ALBEDO line lit); at right the real top view of blue water whose thin pale lines swell into white foam bands as edge_width grows; the pill '13 % foam' lands at the end.
B19.motion_claim: Thin lines swell into white bands as the width grows, and settle at thirteen percent of the surface.
B19.why: The band widening on the real water is the claim, and the coverage number is measured from that same render.

cues.label: roughness: 0 is a mirror, 1 is fully matte

props.caption: foam_roughness 0.15 up to 0.9: the glare on the foam lines fades

B20.capture_spec: C12: scene water_scene.gd, shader 03-noise-foam, foam_roughness swept 0.15 to 0.9 between 15 % and 85 % of the beat.
B20.visual_intent: Code card (ALBEDO, ALPHA, ROUGHNESS lines); the real cove: at first the foam lines streak with the sun's glare like wet paint, then as foam_roughness rises the streaks fade to flat white.
B20.motion_claim: The glare streaks along the foam lines die away as the foam turns matte.
B20.runner_up: manim: a lobe on foam vs water
B20.why: The streaks fading on the real foam is the evidence; the sentence is about a visible artifact.

cues.label: o: where this square's point sits, circling
TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game
density: how many squares fit across the plane

props.caption: cell_speed 0 to 2, then cell_density 10 to 18

B21.capture_spec: C13: scene water_scene.gd, shader 03-noise-foam, cell_speed swept 0 to 2 between 30 % and 60 %, then cell_density 10 to 18 from 62 % to the end.
B21.visual_intent: Code card (the point's offset line and the call line lit in turn); the real cove: the foam net frozen, then breathing faster, then the cells shrinking as the density rises.
B21.motion_claim: The net starts to breathe, speeds up, then the squares shrink.
B21.runner_up: manim: a point circling in its square
B21.why: The real net breathing and tightening is the sentence's motion.

cues.label: pow: x raised to the power y

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · top view · power rises
props.caption: one minus the nearest distance, to a power: a soft dot per point

B22.capture_spec: C14: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, shader 03b-power-curve (clamped), sharpness swept 2 to 10 across the beat, 1080 x 1080.
B22.visual_intent: Code card (the power-curve fragment, the pow line lit); the real top view of blue water with a soft white blob around every point that shrinks to a glitter dot as the power rises; pills 'power 2' then 'power 10'.
B22.motion_claim: Soft white blobs shrink into glitter as the power rises.
B22.runner_up: manim: the curve of one minus d to the power p
B22.why: Two real hold frames of the render, linked by the sweep, show how the power sharpens; a plot would show the function only.

props.code:
float glow = pow(1.0 - c.x, sharpness);
	if (clamped > 0.5) glow = pow(clamp(1.0 - c.x, 0.0, 1.0), sharpness);

cues.label: pow of a negative base is undefined
clamp: pins x inside a range

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · top view · clamp at 55 %
props.caption: 462 of 1,166,400 pixels read exactly black; with the clamp, none

B23.capture_spec: C15: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, shader 03b-power-curve unclamped (sharpness 5, cell_speed 0 so the pattern is frozen and the specks stay put), clamped by --set-at at 55 % of the beat; 1080 x 1080. Ring box = the 258-pixel speck at (221, 545) of the 1080 x 1080 frame (evidence/planning-checks/png/pow-static-broken.png).
B23.visual_intent: Code card (the two glow lines; the unclamped line lit then the clamp line); the real top view with tiny black specks that blink in the first half and are gone after the clamp at 55 %; a terracotta ring around one speck at 30 % and the pill '88 px'.
B23.motion_claim: Black specks blink on the foam, then vanish when the clamp is applied.

show.event: ring on a speck, pill 88 px

B23.runner_up: manim: a negative base on a number line
B23.why: A real speck on the real frame, ringed, with the real pixel count, is stronger than a diagram of why it happens.

props.code:
float edge = texture(cell_tex, UV * cell_scale + vec2(1.0, 0.4) * TIME * scroll_speed).r;
	float foam = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, edge_width, edge);

cues.label: texture: an image a shader can read by address

props.caption: Cellular · fractal off · Seamless

B24.capture_spec: C16: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE top view, left: 03-noise-foam (function), right: 03d-foam-from-texture (a baked cellular NoiseTexture2D: Cellular, return Distance2 Sub, fractal type None, Seamless), both 1080 x 1080 joined side by side. The ring box [0.595, 0.37, 0.735, 0.57] is the smudged cross where the seamless blend shows, read off the recorded frame at 10.5 s (72 % of the estimated beat); the cross scrolls with the texture, so re-read it if the beat length changes by more than a second.
B24.visual_intent: Wide window with the two top views side by side: the function's crisp net (left) and the baked texture's net (right) with a visible smudge in the middle; code excerpt below (the two texture lines); pills '9 hashes' and '1 read'; a ring on the smudge.
B24.motion_claim: The two nets drift side by side; the right one scrolls rigidly and the cells never change shape.
B24.runner_up: manim: a texture tile and a function box
B24.why: Two real nets side by side are the comparison; the smudge is a real artifact the viewer can see.
